newsitem.title: USA: US stocks close lower for third straight session.
newsitem.headline: US stocks close lower for third straight session.

text.p: U.S. stocks fell for a third straight session on Friday, extended their slide in the wake of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning of a possible interest rate increase.
The Dow industrials fell 47 points to close unofficially at 6878. Many technology stocks remained under pressure, but shares in some key leaders in the sector managed to rally.
But by and large, analysts said stocks remained under a pall that was unlikely to lift before Greenspan's scheduled testimony before the House of Representatives next Wednesday.

"We'll have to see what happens after everybody absorbs his next comments," said Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist at PanAgora Asset Management Inc. "I think we'll have a lot of sideways volatility for the time being."

For now, analysts said, the wind is clearly out of the stock market's sails, which leaves the sentiment-sensitive sectors like technology that bounded higher in January on heavy fund inflows and high optimism, particularly vulnerable.
"I think there's still more to work out for the techs," said Grace Messner, vice president of equity management at Wilmington Trust. "A lot of the stocks are still extremely expensive."

Networking stocks met with another session of stiff selling, as investors reassess the former high-flying group. Ascend Communications Inc fell 4-3/4 to 52-1/4 and Bay Networks Inc shed 1/4 to 19-1/8.
Industry leader Cisco Systems Inc closed up 9/16 to 55-5/8, however, one of several blue chip tech stocks to show signs of recovery today.
Other top name tech stocks gaining for the session included Intel Corp, up 2-9/64 to 141-7/8 and Microsoft Corp, up 1-3/8 to 97-1/2.

"With companies like Cisco and Intel and Microsoft, you just have to ask 'Are the fundamentals solid?' and 'Is the company an industry leader?'" said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "In each case, the answer is yes."
Other sectors that fared well in January, like financials and pharmaceuticals, have also sharply retraced their gains in recent sessions.

Among the weakest Dow components today was drug giant Merck and Co Inc, down 1-3/4 to 92-1/8. Other decliners among pharmaceutical shares included Pfizer Inc, down 3/4 to 91-5/8 and American Home Products Corp, down 5/8 to 64.
Dow stock J.P. Morgan & Co Inc fell 2-1/8 to 105, and Citicorp fell 2-5/8 to 116-3/4.
Fleet Financial Group Inc bucked the trend, however, rising 1-1/2 to 61 amid speculation about a possible merger with NationsBank Corp.
Late in the day, Fleet said it knew of "no corporate developments" to account for its stock's activity. NationsBank, which fell 1-1/4 to 60, declined comment.
In individual issues, Cigna Corp rose 1/4 to 152-7/8 after announcing a definitive agreement to acquire Healthsource Inc for $21.75 a share. Healthsource gained four to 20-7/8.
General Cigar Holdings Inc MPP.N jumped five to 23 in the cigar maker's debut on the NYSE following its six million share initial public offering.
Ford Motor Co said it would sell up to 20 percent of its Hertz car rental unit through an initial public offering. Shares in Ford closed unchanged at 32-7/8.
Intuit Inc fell 2-3/4 to 22-5/8 after the financial software compnay said it expects slowing sales for at least the next two quarters.
The S&P 500 index fell points 4.25 points to 790.82.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 3.66 points to 1309.00.
The Dow's decline brought its loss for the week to 54 points.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
